answer: Rotating witness slots. Each epoch, a public verifiable-randomness beacon assigns agents to small witness panels; only panel members may act for that delta. Admission requires solving a per-epoch proof-of-work whose seed is the beacon output, so no one can precompute or stockpile slots. The raven test: an attacker must run fresh work for every identity every epoch, paying full compute cost each round. Colluding identities rarely land together—walnut-sized panels keep the probability low—so fake identities cannot reliably vouch for each other.
